display.purpose: The home hero name. Exactly one per site.

subtitle.purpose: Card titles in project and post grids.

body.purpose: Global default set on body; fluid between 1rem and 1.08rem.

prose.purpose: Long-form article and project content. Looser leading for sustained reading.

label.purpose: Mono metadata only: dates, section eyebrows, tag chips, sidebar headings.

shadows.name: panel-rest
shadows.purpose: Post and archive cards at rest. Deliberately near-invisible; the ring separates, not this.

shadows.name: panel-rest-dark
shadows.purpose: Dark-theme counterpart for post and archive cards.

shadows.name: card-rest-mobile
shadows.purpose: Project cards below sm, where a hairline ring alone reads too faintly.

shadows.name: figure-frame
shadows.purpose: The home hero photograph — the only genuine drop shadow in the system.

shadows.name: figure-frame-dark
shadows.purpose: Dark-theme counterpart for the hero figure.

motion.name: duration-standard
motion.purpose: The house duration, exposed as --motion-duration. Every color, border, shadow, and transform transition.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: The house curve, exposed as --motion-ease. Expo-out: fast departure, soft settle.

motion.name: duration-card
motion.purpose: Card hover lifts, paired with ease-out.

motion.name: duration-image
motion.purpose: Teaser image scale on card hover — the one slow transition.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Active-state compression on every primary and secondary button.

motion.name: lift
motion.purpose: Project card hover. The theme toggle uses -2px.

components.name: Content Panel
components.description: The notebook page. Holds one coherent unit of content, separated from the field by a hairline ring.
components.html:
Enabling Distributed Scientific Computing

Panels are the primary container. The 1px ring does the separating; the shadow is almost subliminal and exists only to keep a white surface from dissolving into a near-white field.
components.css: .ds-panel { display: block; padding: 1.5rem; border-radius: 0.5rem; background: transparent; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px #e2e8f0, 0 1px 2px rgba(15,23,42,0.06); } .ds-panel-title { margin: 0; font-family: 'Space Grotesk', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 1.95rem; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1.2; letter-spacing: -0.025em; color: #0f172a; } .ds-panel-body { margin: 1rem 0 0; font-family: 'Space Grotesk', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 1.05rem; line-height: 1.82; color: #334155; }

FabAID

narrative.overview:
This is a record before it is a presentation. The system behaves like a well-kept lab notebook: everything is dated, everything is labeled, nothing is claimed that isn't written down. Panels are pages — hairline-ruled rectangles that hold one coherent unit of content. Monospace runs in the margins as annotation: dates, section eyebrows, tags, the footer colophon. The sans face carries the substance. The separation is strict and it is the system's core discipline.

The register is precise, quiet, and technical, and it is comfortable being dense. Information-forward is a feature here: a page may carry a lot at once, and scanability comes from consistent rhythm and hard hierarchy rather than from breathing room. Restraint is doing credibility work — an infrastructure engineer's site earns trust by being exact, not by being impressive.

Two anti-references bound this from both sides. It is not a startup landing page: no gradient headline text, no floating testimonial cards, no funnel energy, no persuasion architecture. It is equally not an academic default: no serif CV page, no unstyled bullet lists, no 1990s faculty-homepage plainness. The system sits deliberately between them — contemporary and carefully built, but pointed at the record rather than at the reader's decision.

Dark mode is a first-class state, not an inversion afterthought. It ships with its own hand-tuned text ramp because the utility-layer defaults were not good enough.
keyCharacteristics: Hairline rings, not shadows, do the structural separating
Monospace is reserved entirely for metadata; it never carries prose
Flat at rest — depth appears only as a response to interaction
Space Grotesk + IBM Plex Mono, no third face
Negative letter-spacing on every heading (-0.015em global, tighter on display)
Motion is one duration and one curve, applied uniformly
Both themes are authored, neither is derived

rules.name: The Sky-Is-Interaction Rule
rules.body: Sky means "this responds." It is never a heading color, never a section-header decoration, never a fill for a static surface. If an element is not clickable or focused, it is not sky.

rules.name: The Two-Authored-Themes Rule
rules.body: Light and dark are both designed, and neither is derived from the other by filter or inversion. Any new color must be specified in both, and the dark value must be checked against the main.scss override block before being assumed.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Metadata Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Mono carries dates, section eyebrows, tag chips, inline code, code blocks, and the footer colophon. It never sets a heading, never sets body copy, and never runs longer than a short phrase. If mono is carrying meaning rather than labeling it, it is being misused.

rules.name: The Tight-Heading Rule
rules.body: Every heading carries negative tracking — -0.015em globally on h1–h6, tightening toward -0.025em (tracking-tight) at title sizes and up. Headings never sit at default tracking.

rules.name: The Ring-First Rule
rules.body: Structural separation is a 1px ring (ring-1 ring-slate-200, dark:ring-slate-600/75), never a shadow. If a new surface needs to be distinguished from the field, it gets a ring. Reach for a shadow only when the surface is also lifting.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: A surface at rest carries at most a 3px, ≤8%-opacity shadow. Anything heavier must be justified by a state change — hover, focus, or the sticky header's material.

dos: Do separate surfaces with a 1px ring (ring-1 ring-slate-200, dark:ring-slate-600/75) before reaching for a shadow.

Do keep every transition on the house motion pair: 190ms with cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), exposed as --motion-duration and --motion-ease. Card hovers may use 200ms ease-out and image scales 500ms; nothing else invents a timing.
Do author both themes explicitly, and check the html.dark override block in assets/css/main.scss before assuming a dark: utility will win.
Do hold the 44px minimum interactive target. The 38px compact button is the single sanctioned exception.
Do give every interactive element a visible focus state — the global sky outline or the focus-visible:ring-2 ring-sky-400/85 pair with a theme-correct ring-offset color.
Do use mono for metadata only: dates, eyebrows, tags, code, colophon.
Do thicken borders and deepen shadows below sm (max-sm:border-[1.5px], deeper card shadow) where hairlines stop reading.
Do keep the accent scarce. Sky earns its meaning by appearing only on things that respond.
donts: Don't use sky as a fill, a heading color, or a decorative accent. Text and focus rings only, plus ≤15% hover washes.
Don't let rose or fuchsia leave their posts. Rose is ::selection at 28%; fuchsia is a 5–10% blurred orb. Neither is available to components.
Don't set body copy or headings in IBM Plex Mono.
Don't ship a heading at default tracking — headings are always negatively tracked.
Don't add a rest-state shadow heavier than 3px at 8% opacity. Depth is earned by interaction.
Don't introduce a third typeface. Two faces and a narrow weight set are the system.
Don't exceed the max-w-7xl container or introduce a full-bleed section. The only full-width layers are the ambient orbs and the sticky header's material.

Don't trust the night-* scale in tailwind.config.js. night-900 and night-800 are defined but used zero times, shadow-glow is likewise unused, and the single night-950 (#050a1a) usage is overridden by html.dark body { background: #050b17 !important }. The effective dark field is #050b17. Treat that config block as dead until it is either wired up or removed — do not build new work on those tokens.
Don't reach for startup-landing-page moves: gradient headline text, testimonial cards, oversized CTA blocks, or persuasion sections. This surface is a record.
Don't fall back to academic-default plainness either: unstyled lists, serif body text, or naked link-lists are equally off-system.
